transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SA), Elaine Park (Redwood CSM); Michael Chen (SummitBank Sec Eng), Lisa Morales (SummitBank Platform), Rajiv Singh (SummitBank IT), Hannah Wu (SummitBank Compliance)

Summary (auto):
Quick security review focused on SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning, mapping groups to RBAC roles and least-privilege model. Discussed audit logs, retention, KMS/encryption, data residency for EU customers, and SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: share SCIM guide, RBAC matrix template, SOC2 link, and schedule pilot sync.

Topics: SAML SSO setup, SCIM provisioning, RBAC role mapping, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, data residency, SOC2/ISO references

Transcript: (transcription has some noise, names sometimes mis-attributed)
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time the week before new years. Uh just quick agenda, we'll run through SSO SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, then Priya will take into RBAC mapping and least privilege, and then we'll touch audit logs and encryption. Any must-have items on your side?
[00:28] Michael Chen: Yeah thanks Jordan. Uh the big questions from our side are, number one, how automated is SCIM provisioning with groups, two how do we map to the least-privilege roles — the usual, and three audit log retention and whether logs can go to our SIEM. Also, data residency — we have EU tenants and need EU-only data at rest.
[00:48] Jordan Lee: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Quick intro, Priya is our SE who owns auth and provisioning flows, Marco is the architect who owns encryption details.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Hi all. So starting at a high level, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. In practice, customers use Okta or Azure AD, and we have pre-built connectors for both. Quick note: the connector expects group soft-mapping — so you can push group membership and we will map groups to roles.
[01:32] Lisa Morales: When you say "map groups to roles", is that a one-time sync or live? We want near real-time but not immediate spikes.
[01:43] Priya Nair: It's a provisioning sync — SCIM calls trigger provisioning events. We do continuous polling on our side for SCIM delta, so typical latency is under a minute for membership changes in normal load. If you want immediate, we can support push events but that's custom.
[02:05] Rajiv Singh: Are there rate limits? We have a big org, 10k users, a couple hundred groups.
[02:13] Priya Nair: Yes there are sensible rate limits; we'll share the exact numbers in the SCIM guide. For very large orgs we recommend batched syncs or a pilot to tune rate throttles.
[02:27] Michael Chen: Ok fine. On SAML, can we configure assertion attributes to include group claims? Our requirement is IdP sends groups and email, and we need to enforce email domain validation.
[02:40] Marco Diaz: SAML assertions support group claims; we accept standard attributes and you can map them to Redwood roles in the admin console. For email domain we have a validation rule — you can restrict allowed domains and enforce MFA upstream.
[02:54] Hannah Wu: Anything about SCIM de-provisioning? We need immediate access revocation when someone leaves.
[03:02] Priya Nair: Yes SCIM supports de-provisioning (active -> inactive). De-provisioning is processed immediately; access tokens are revoked. There is a caveat if there are long LROs or active sessions, but we actively invalidate sessions on de-provisioning in our Dedicated and Private modes. Hosted has a short TTL we enforce.
[03:29] Michael Chen: SSO metadata — do you support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? We run both.
[03:37] Jordan Lee: Yes both. We provide SAML metadata XML for SP and can consume IdP metadata; we'll walk through metadata exchange in the guide.
[03:46] Lisa Morales: Ok good. Now RBAC — how fine-grained is your role model? We have least-privilege needs: some teams should only be able to run inference, others can change models/rollouts and billing but not view secrets.
[04:01] Priya Nair: We have a base role model: viewer, operator, admin, billing. It maps to actions like model-deploy, config-edit, view-logs, manage-keys. For Private deployments we expose more granular roles; for Hosted you can create custom roles via the Console and map SCIM groups to custom roles. We'll share an RBAC matrix.
[04:25] Rajiv Singh: Can you restrict token generation to certain roles? We want only ops to mint service tokens, not devs.
[04:32] Marco Diaz: Yes tokens are scoped by role. We also support short-lived tokens and per-token scopes. For extra safety we integrate with KMS for envelope encryption and key control.
[04:46] Michael Chen: Ok interesting, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM?
[04:52] Marco Diaz: We support CMK via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS and GCP KMS; HSM-backed keys are available for Private on-prem deployments. We'll send the crypto whitepaper.
[05:09] Hannah Wu: Data residency — we have EU and US business units. Can we pin data to regions?
[05:17] Jordan Lee: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted, we have EU regions with at-rest encryption and logs stored in EU. For Dedicated/Private you can ensure all data and logs remain in your VPC or on-prem.
[05:30] Michael Chen: Audit logs: retention windows, export, and SIEM integration? We need 1 year retention, S3 export and syslog to Splunk.
[05:40] Marco Diaz: Audit logs are retained per your plan; we support configurable retention up to several years. You can export to S3 buckets and integrate with syslog/forwarders; we also provide webhooks and a streaming API for logs to ship them to Splunk. We'll include the API docs.
[05:58] Lisa Morales: Do you provide immutable logs for compliance?
[06:03] Priya Nair: For Dedicated/Private, you can configure write-once storage or ship logs to your own immutable store. Hosted offers append-only logs with tamper-evidence features.
[06:17] Michael Chen: SOC 2 artifacts — do you share type II report? We need to review them with legal.
[06:23] Elaine Park: Yes we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates. I'll upload them to the deal folder and send a link.
[06:31] Hannah Wu: Regarding RBAC least privilege mapping, can you show an example of group-to-role mapping?
[06:37] Priya Nair: Sure, quick example: SCIM group 'rbac-inference-run' -> role 'operator' (can run jobs, not deploy). 'rbac-model-admins' -> role 'admin' (deploy, rollback). We can also map attributes like department:billing to the 'billing' role.
[06:56] Rajiv Singh: Any way to enforce separation of duties — e.g., model promotion requires 2 approvers?
[07:05] Marco Diaz: We have approval workflows — you can require multi-approver rollouts in the Console for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we provide webhooks to integrate with your approval engine.
[07:17] Michael Chen: How about SCIM schema customization — a few of our apps have custom attributes like cost_center. Can we sync those?
[07:27] Priya Nair: Yes SCIM allows custom attributes; we'll show sample manifest and mapping rules.
[07:36] Lisa Morales: If a user's email changes, will you automatically remap identity or create a duplicate account? We hit that with other vendors.
[07:45] Priya Nair: We recommend you use immutable user IDs (externalId) for SCIM so email changes don't create duplicates. If you only rely on email, we can configure merge rules but it's fragile. We will document a recommended best-practice.
[08:00] Michael Chen: Ok good. On the logging side, what fields are available in audit logs — do you include token_id, actor, action, resource, IP, and full request payload?
[08:10] Marco Diaz: We log actor, actor_role, token_id (hashed), action, resource path, request metadata including IP and user-agent. Full request payload is logged in a redactable field — we mask PII by default and can include full payloads in Private deployments if you need them for debugging.
[08:33] Hannah Wu: GDPR question — data subject access requests and deletion: can you purge user data including embeddings if needed?
[08:42] Jordan Lee: We support data deletion workflows. For embeddings we treat them as derived data; we support purging related records and regenerating cache. For EU data residency we ensure deletion requests are executed in the region of origin. We'll share the DSAR playbook.
[09:00] Michael Chen: Is there an SLA around deletion? We need confirmed deletion within 30 days for certain data classes.
[09:07] Marco Diaz: Our standard is 30 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private can match shorter SLAs under contract. We'll add that to the SLA doc we send.
[09:19] Lisa Morales: Encryption at rest and in transit — what ciphers and key lengths?
[09:24] Marco Diaz: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; AES-256-GCM for at rest. We also support envelope encryption with RSA-2048/4096 or EC keys via KMS. Detailed cipher suites are in the crypto whitepaper.
[09:41] Rajiv Singh: For forensic needs, can we pull historical logs older than retention for a pay-per-access?
[09:49] Marco Diaz: Yes you can request extended retention or on-demand archive retrieval. There may be cost for long-term storage retrieval.
[09:58] Michael Chen: Any concerns around SCIM provisioning causing accidental mass changes? We want guardrails.
[10:05] Priya Nair: The Console has preview mode for SCIM changes and dry-run APIs. We also support allowlists, and for large changes we recommend pilot runs and rate limits.
[10:18] Lisa Morales: Ok that's helpful. A few picky items from compliance: we need SAML assertion expiration <= 5 minutes and audience restrictions enforced.
[10:26] Jordan Lee: Those are standard; you can configure assertion lifetime and audience in SAML config.
[10:33] Hannah Wu: How do you surface who changed RBAC mappings and when?
[10:38] Marco Diaz: Audit logs show who changed roles and the before/after. For Dedicated you can integrate with SIEM and get immutable records.
[10:47] Michael Chen: One last thing — keys in logs: we don't want secrets in logs.
[10:52] Priya Nair: We redact secrets by default and strip known token patterns. In Private you can control logging behavior fully.
[11:02] Jordan Lee: Great — quick recap, we'll share the SCIM provisioning guide and sample manifest, RBAC matrix template, SOC2/ISO artifacts, crypto whitepaper, and DSAR playbook. Michael to provide SAML metadata and pilot groups. We'll set up a pilot week of Jan 11.
[11:20] Michael Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:25] Lisa Morales: Thanks, appreciate the detail.
[11:28] Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with links.

(End of transcript)
